title: The Italian Renaissance
subtitle: 14th-16th century
subject: art
description: In two centuries, Italy reinvented painting, sculpture and architecture, and changed the way we see the world.

hero.hook: In two centuries, Italy has reinvented art and our way of looking at the world.

blocks.text: The Italian Renaissance (14th-16th century) is not just a change in style. It's a new way of seeing the world. In two centuries, Italy placed observation, reason and the individual at the center of everything.

Born in the rich cities of the peninsula, this revolution reinvents painting, sculpture and architecture. Two driving forces are driving it: the rediscovery of Greek and Roman Antiquity, and daring technical inventions.

sections.title: Florence, the city that lights the fuse

blocks.text: It all starts in **Florence**, which dominated the European economy in the 14th century thanks to textiles and banking. The **Medici** family took power there. These bankers use [[Patronage]], artist financing, as a prestige tool.
To get around the ban on lending with interest, the Medici invented banking tricks. The Church turns a blind eye as long as they finance chapels.

blocks.caption: Laurent de Medici, known as “the Magnificent”, great protector of artists.

blocks.text: At the same time, **humanism** changes the place of man. Thinkers like [[Mirandola Peak]] assert that human beings are capable of understanding nature through reason. In **1453**, the fall of Constantinople pushes scholars to Italy with forgotten Greek manuscripts.

sections.title: Painting the real: perspective and body

blocks.text: In the 15th century, the architect **Brunelleschi** invented the [[Linear perspective in painting]] around **1420**. Gone are the Middle Ages, where what was more important was painted larger: space now follows mathematical rules, like a window open to reality.

blocks.caption: Perspective gives the illusion of depth on a flat surface.

blocks.text: **Leonardo da Vinci** goes further: he dissects bodies to understand muscles and nerves, and also paint emotions. Oil paint, coming from Flanders, gradually replaces [[Tempera]] and allows [[Chiaroscuro]]: these contrasts of shadow and light which give relief.
The body that Leonardo studied most was that of a hundred year old man. Examining it, he described one of the first known cases of an artery blocked by age.

At the beginning of the 16th century, Rome took the place of Florence, carried by building popes like **Julius II**. This is the era of the “complete man”. **Leonardo da Vinci** is the model: painter, engineer, anatomist.
**Michelangelo** embodies strength. His **David** becomes the symbol of Florence. Between **1508** and **1512**, he painted the ceiling of the **Sistine Chapel**: 500 square meters on Genesis.

blocks.caption: Michelangelo, from David on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.

blocks.text: In *The Last Judgment*, Michelangelo painted his own face on flayed skin: a way of expressing how much this work had exhausted him.
**Raphaël** embodies grace. His fresco *The School of Athens* brings together the great thinkers of Antiquity in a harmony that will serve as a model for centuries.

After the death of Raphaël in **1520**, the balance is disrupted. The artists elongate the bodies and force the colors: this is [[Mannerism]], a more restless art. The King of France **Francis I** invited Leonardo and launched the **French Renaissance**, with the castles of the Loire.

blocks.text: Born in Florence thanks to the Medici, the Italian Renaissance revolutionized art with perspective (around 1420) and the study of the body, before reaching its peak in Rome with Leonardo, Michelangelo and Raphael.
